notes.kya: For eki- nouns: ekika kya Ffumbe, the clan of the civet cat.
notes.gwa: For omu- (things) nouns: omuziro gwa…, the totem of…
notes.ndi-wa: Ndi wa Lugave: I am of the Lugave clan.

guidebook.intro: Every Muganda belongs to a clan, passed down from the father. Clans shape names, marriage, ceremonies and even what people eat.

tips.title: Clan and totem
body: A clan, **ekika**, is a large family that traces itself to one ancestor. Each clan has a main totem, **omuziro**, usually an animal or plant, and many take their name from it: the **Ffumbe** clan’s totem is the civet cat, **Lugave**’s is the pangolin.
Members respect their totem and do not eat it. People of the same clan count as relatives, **abooluganda**, and traditionally may not marry each other.

tips.title: “Of” agrees with the first noun
body: “Of” is **-a** with the class prefix of the thing owned: **ekika kya Mmamba** (the clan of Mmamba), **omuziro gwa Ngeye** (the totem of Ngeye), **essaati ya Nakato** (Nakato’s shirt), **omwana wa Mukasa** (Mukasa’s child).

culture.title: Clan names
body: Many Ganda names belong to a particular clan, so a name can tell people your clan before you say it. Buganda has over fifty clans, each led by a clan head, **omutaka**.
